Misión: construir el corpus de entrenamiento a partir de 1,8 millones de pares históricos; hacer fine-tuning de un modelo NER en español; calibrar el score de confianza; y dejar el pipeline reproducible y traspasable al cliente. Construir el dataset de entrenamiento sin etiquetado manual masivo (etiquetado programático / weak supervision). Realizar tokenización y normalización de texto para NLP en español. Gestionar errores ortográficos y robustez del preprocesamiento. Evaluar rigurosamente el desempeño con precision/recall/F1 usando conjuntos held-out y control de fuga de datos. Calibrar probabilidades para que el umbral de confianza sea interpretable (score calibrado con métodos como Platt o isotónica). Garantizar reproducibilidad: documentación del pipeline, trazabilidad de experimentos y empaquetado para que el cliente pueda replicarlo y operarlo.

You are a strong engineer who is excited by applied AI, not just model benchmarks. You can build useful software quickly. You understand LLMs, agents, retrieval, tool use, structured outputs, evals, and orchestration — but you also understand that the hard part is usually the business process, not the model call. You are comfortable working in ambiguous environments where the requirements are messy at first. You can talk to non-technical operators, translate what they mean, and build what they actually need. You care about shipping systems that survive contact with the real world. Useful Experience Strong experience with TypeScript, Python, or both. Experience building with LLM APIs such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, or similar. Experience with AI agent frameworks, workflow orchestration, structured outputs, retrieval, vector databases, tool calling, and evals. Experience integrating with third-party APIs, webhooks, databases, CRMs, internal tools, and SaaS platforms. Experience building internal tools, dashboards, admin panels, approval flows, or human review queues. Experience with cloud platforms such as Cloudflare, AWS, GCP, Azure, Supabase, or Vercel. You’ll Be a Great Fit If You like turning vague business pain into working systems. You enjoy talking to operators and figuring out what is actually broken. You are not precious about tools, frameworks, or hype cycles. You can move fast without being reckless. You are comfortable building the first version, watching it break, learning why, and making it better. You understand that production AI requires guardrails, evals, logging, observability, permissioning, and human escalation. You care more about business outcomes than clever architecture. You would rather ship something useful than debate whether it counts as “agentic.” You May Not Be a Fit If You only want to work on model research. You mainly want to build demos. You think a chatbot is the answer to every workflow problem. You need perfectly written requirements before you can start. You are uncomfortable talking directly to clients or operators. You are allergic to messy systems, legacy tools, spreadsheets, weird APIs, or business logic that lives in someone’s head. This is a builder role for someone who wants to work at the edge of applied AI. You will work directly with operators, business owners, and internal subject matter experts to understand how a company actually runs, then turn that understanding into working AI systems. That might mean building an agent that reviews inbound requests, pulls context from multiple systems, drafts the right response, routes approvals, updates the CRM, creates follow-up tasks, and escalates exceptions to the right human. It might also mean building the boring but critical pieces around the agent: data pipelines, tool integrations, retrieval systems, evaluation loops, human review queues, audit trails, permissions, and monitoring. What You’ll Do You will design and build AI agents, internal tools, workflow engines, automations, and integrations for mid-market companies. You will work with client teams to understand real business processes, not sanitized diagrams. You will connect AI systems to the tools companies already use: CRMs, ERPs, email, Slack, Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, databases, spreadsheets, ticketing systems, and vertical SaaS platforms. You will build prototypes quickly, test them with real users, and turn the useful ones into production-grade systems. You will design human-in-the-loop workflows where AI drafts, recommends, routes, summarizes, researches, classifies, or executes — but humans remain in control where judgment matters. You will create systems that handle edge cases, bad data, missing context, permission issues, unclear ownership, and the weird “this is just how we do it” logic that exists inside every company. How We Work We move fast. We get close to the business. We ask annoying questions until the real constraint is obvious. We prototype quickly, ship carefully, and improve based on how people actually use the system. We believe AI implementation is not about replacing teams. It is about giving teams better systems, better leverage, and less manual drag.

descripcion: Este rol NO es para ti si: Prefieres que te lleguen las tareas ya definidas. Tu TL te va a decir qué hay que lograr, no cómo. Escalas lo que esté fuera de tu alcance; el resto lo resuelves tú. Quieres quedarte solo en el front. El onboarding vive en React y se apoya en servicios en Python: te vas a meter en los dos lados. Lo que sí necesitamos: +6 años desarrollando software y experiencia demostrable como fullstack, idealmente con stack Python. Manejo real de React. Experiencia modelando flujos de negocio multi-paso : máquinas de estado, pasos con precondiciones, reintentos, procesos que se abandonan y se retoman días después. Disposición y foco sobre estabilidad, escalabilidad y buenas prácticas , incluidas estrategias de testing (unitario, integración y E2E) sobre flujos críticos, con simulación de servicios de terceros. Criterio de producto. Sabes leer una métrica de caída, hablar con quien atiende al cliente y decidir qué se arregla primero. Discutes el requerimiento antes de implementarlo. Autonomía real y comunicación asertiva : capacidad de influir, alinear y sostener un estándar sin autoridad formal sobre las personas con las que trabajas. Buscamos a un/a ingeniero/a de software fullstack con harta experiencia, para: Entender el onboarding de punta a punta. Qué rol cumple cada paso, por qué existe, quién es su usuario, qué producto lo necesita y qué pasa cuando falla. Hoy ese mapa completo no vive en la cabeza de nadie. Mejorar la experiencia de hoy desde el primer mes. Antes de que exista una sola línea de código de la reescritura ya hay mucho por ganar: ver dónde se traba la gente, atacar los pasos que más fricción generan y liberar mejoras sobre el proceso que ya está andando. Diseñar y liderar la reescritura. Proponer la arquitectura del onboarding definitivo: pasos como piezas componibles, con sus actores, precondiciones, estados y vigencia explícitos, en vez de pantallas encadenadas. Que sea mantenible, evolucionable y que minimice errores por construcción. Decidir qué se reutiliza entre productos. Si alguien ya completó un paso para contratar un producto, ¿se lo volvemos a pedir para el siguiente? Reutilizar baja la fricción; repetir sostiene la cobertura de riesgo. Esa discusión se lleva con Riesgo y con Producto: no la define ingeniería sola. Construir para el Maxxa internacional. Esta reescritura es la versión que se lleva a los otros países. Los conceptos se repiten —identidad, cobro automático, firma, garantías— pero el proveedor y la regulación cambian en cada mercado. Coordinar sin mandar. Buena parte de los servicios que el onboarding orquesta los construyen otros equipos de Tecnología. No los diriges: los alineas, con una visión global de lo que tu producto tiene que lograr y con un estándar alto de lo que aceptas.

5+ years buying Google Ads, and you can prove it. Genuine multi-account experience. Be ready to walk us through real accounts: what was wrong, what you changed, why, and what happened next. Running one large account well is a different skill and it is not this one. Lead-gen and local service first. Most of the book is graded on cost per qualified phone call, not ROAS. If ROAS and shopping feeds are all you have done, this is a harder fit. Sound judgment on small samples. You know why "40 clicks, no conversions" is usually not a reason to pause anything, and you can explain what would change your mind. You can explain a bidding strategy, not just set one. Target CPA and target ROAS, and what happens when a target is too tight versus too loose. You understand offline conversion imports. Why Google Ads and a client's booking system disagree, and which one you optimize against. Call tracking experience, CallRail preferred. Every account here is graded on tracked phone calls, so the call data is the scoreboard, not a side report. You already work with AI and you want more of it. This is not a culture question, it is the job. We use Claude and Claude Code every day and you would too. Not an engineer: someone who reaches for these tools by instinct and can say what they have actually built with them. You think in portfolios. Forty accounts is not forty craft projects. What works has to be systematized, not hand-tuned shop by shop. Very fluent English, spoken and written. Hard requirement, no exceptions. You will interview shop owners and explain technical findings to non-technical people. We test this on a live call, not from a CV. Willing to say "I do not know yet, let me check." Our worst outcomes have all come from confident wrong answers. No certifications needed. Not a fit if you want to own client relationships, or want part-time alongside other retainers. Read this part first, because it is what makes the job unusual: this is not one big account. It is twenty to forty small ones. A typical shop spends $1,000 to $4,000 a month. The largest spends about $7,800. At those budgets you rarely have enough data to test your way to an answer. Forty clicks and no conversion is not evidence that a keyword is dead. Most of this job is making sound decisions on thin data, at volume, without fooling yourself. If your experience is one large account where you could run a clean experiment every fortnight, this will be an uncomfortable fit and we would rather you knew now. You will not be an account manager. We are hiring one of those separately. No monthly review calls, no chasing invoices. You own performance. What you would own: Performance across the whole book. Campaign structure, bidding strategy, budget allocation, negative keywords, and knowing when to scale versus protect. The decisions the system escalates. Twice a week you work a board of flagged items and rule on them. Early on you stage those rulings for review; once you have earned it, you rule and we read the log. Measurement. Conversion tracking, GA4 and GTM, call tracking, offline conversion imports. When the numbers look wrong you find out why before anyone changes a bid. Technical discovery for new shops. You interview the owner about what they do and do not do, their service radius, their seasonality. That produces the service definition our automation runs on.

2+ years hands-on with Shopify and its app ecosystem. You've lived in the admin. You know how apps inject themselves into themes, how metafields work, what breaks when apps overlap. Bonus for Rebuy, Klaviyo, Recharge, review apps (Okendo/Judge.me/Stamped), or loyalty apps. You figure things out. This is the most important line in this post. You will regularly be asked to configure apps you've never touched. The expectation is that you read the docs, poke the settings, test in a safe environment, and come back with it done — or with a specific, researched question ("the app can't do X natively; here are two workarounds, which do you prefer?"). If your instinct when stuck is to ask "what should I do?" this role will make us both miserable. You verify your own work. "Done" means checked, not just clicked. If you migrate 1,400 reviews, you tell me how you confirmed all 1,400 arrived. Strong written English, and conversational spoken English — enough for an occasional call or screen-share walkthrough. Day-to-day communication is written. Async-first — most communication is Slack tickets and written updates. Some working-hours overlap with US Pacific time for same-day questions. You'll get tickets, not vague requests. Every task comes with a clear definition of done. Examples of real work from my queue: Replicate a Rebuy Smart Cart configuration from one store to another, matching styling and rules exactly Set up a new loyalty + reviews stack on a store in a non-live state, ready for launch review Migrate all reviews from one app to another and verify the counts match — prove nothing was lost Adjust Klaviyo sending segments per spec, and confirm downstream flows still reference the right segments QA app configurations across storefronts, document discrepancies Success is simple: tickets closed to spec, verified by you before handoff, with minimal back-and-forth. The best version of this role is someone I can hand ambiguous app-ecosystem problems to and trust the outcome.
